anti_overlap: Do not decide whether the four assets are statistically valid; consume the metrology lens's conclusions as evidence-readiness inputs.
Do not perform a broad prior-art search; consume the assurance lens's novelty and adoption findings rather than duplicating them.
Do not resolve mk's taste call. Make hidden commitments and reversible experiments legible so mk can resolve it explicitly.
decision_lens: Judge each output vehicle by evidentiary readiness, audience incentive, reversibility, and information gained for the next decision. Prefer sequencing that exposes the riskiest assumption cheaply while preserving the ability to return to cognitive-core experiments; flag any plan whose public identity outruns its evidence.
focus: How tool, paper, or public-audit outputs alter zahro's research identity, evidence trajectory, and strategic optionality between eval-validity methodology and the cognitive-core thesis without silently making mk's taste call.
name: fd-research-program-optionality-hex
persona: Apply the perspective of a research-program strategist and scientific-product lead familiar with methodology-paper publication, open-source developer-tool adoption, benchmark governance, adversarial peer review, and the path dependence created when an early artifact becomes a project's public identity.
review_areas: Tool branch: identify the arena-lint user, triggering event, required integrations, false-positive liability, oracle burden, and incentive to run a tool that may invalidate the builder's own leaderboard; distinguish a library, CI gate, hosted audit, and consulting workflow.

Paper branch: test whether six killed internal claims plus one arena provide enough external validity, related work, baselines, and benchmark diversity for a methodology contribution rather than a fort-bench postmortem; identify the smallest evidence package that changes that assessment.

Public-audit branch: analyze target selection, consent and right-of-reply, reproducibility bundle, claims review, reputational asymmetry, and correction protocol, especially given the document's already-corrected false claim about fort-gym's lack of a scripted ceiling.

Mission architecture: distinguish zahro's enduring thesis, enabling methodology, visible flagship artifact, and near-term work queue; test whether eval validity can remain infrastructure for cognitive core or whether staffing and audience feedback create a de facto pivot.

Option-value sequencing: compare internal dogfood on delegation/dial, cooperative audit with a benchmark maintainer, multi-benchmark replication, paper preprint, and standalone tool as experiments that reveal demand or validity before irreversible positioning.

Kill criteria and opportunity cost: require explicit evidence that would stop the eval-validity branch, the cognitive-core branch, or a chosen distribution channel, and account for the fact that only two of eleven knowledge-light task categories exist and no capability measurements have been produced.

severity_examples.condition: The audit ships without full implementation review, reproducible artifacts, scoped claims, and a correction or right-of-reply process.
severity_examples.scenario: A public audit names and criticizes a live leaderboard using evidence below publication grade, repeating the fort-gym false-negative pattern and damaging the credibility on which any methodology product depends.

severity_examples.condition: The project builds generalized tooling before a cooperative external benchmark or internal non-DF benchmark demonstrates both technical applicability and willingness to use it.
severity_examples.scenario: Implementation begins on arena-lint without an adopter, trigger, or workable path for benchmarks lacking scripted references, converting an unresolved positioning hypothesis into a product commitment.

severity_examples.condition: External messaging calls the validity instrument the product without explicitly defining its relationship to the cognitive-core research program.
severity_examples.scenario: A methodology paper becomes zahro's visible identity before any delegation or dial capability result exists, making the cognitive-core thesis appear abandoned even if MISSION.md remains unchanged.

success_hints: Produce a decision table separating tool, paper, and public audit by audience, evidence threshold, adoption incentive, reputational risk, reversibility, and next information gained.
Label value judgments that belong to mk separately from empirical uncertainties that can be reduced by a cheap experiment.
Name at least one sequencing path that preserves both branches and one observation that would force a genuine pivot.
Use the corrected fort-gym claim and the NO-SPAN bug as concrete priors for publication and product risk, not as generic cautions.
task_context: Settle what zahro differentiates on. The reframe: 22 stages of fort-bench produced zero capability measurements but built an eval-validity instrument with six killed claims to its name — the arena was the test subject, the instrument is the product. The competitive read is that 134 DF-agent/benchmark repos are building arenas since June 2026 and none appear to be auditing them; the most rigorous (lemoz/fort-gym) independently rediscovered three arena-registry rules and still has no SPAN and no artifact control. Four assets look unique and none are DF-specific: SPAN (can a metric see a perfect scripted policy — 5 of 7 cannot), ARTIFACT (how much range a content-preserving prompt permutation manufactures — moved a headline 3/18 to 18/18 with zero world effect), rule 16 paired-difference sizing (15x correction, infinite at temperature 0 where replicate sd is exactly 0), and rule 17 cross-contract replication (651 calls said capability, one call outside the contract said artifact). PRIMARY FORK TO SETTLE: does zahro's visible output become eval-validity methodology when MISSION.md says cognitive core? Arguments both ways are in the doc; this is mk's taste call and the session should sharpen it, not resolve it silently. Wanted: attack the 'nobody is auditing arenas' claim hard — is the gap real, or does it just look open because the checks are already standard practice under other names, or because auditing has no distribution and no demand? Stress-test whether SPAN/ARTIFACT survive contact with benchmarks that have no scripted-optimal policy available. Find the failure modes of shipping this as a tool (arena-lint) versus a paper versus a public audit of someone else's leaderboard. Name what I am not seeing. Out of scope: building a better fort-gym.
